inputs.name: clitarget
inputs.intent: Books can be imported and exported as delimited text, read with clitarget's own reader, not a second one. POST /books/import takes a delimited-text body whose header is title,isbn, in clitarget's FIELD SYNTAX; every row is validated as POST /books validates a book. When every row is valid the books are created in file order and the answer is HTTP 201 with the JSON body {"imported": <n>}. When any row is invalid or has the wrong number of fields the answer is HTTP 400 with the JSON body {"message": "<reason>"} and no book is created. GET /books/export answers HTTP 200 with the header title,isbn and one row per book in the order GET /books lists them, a field quoted in clitarget's FIELD SYNTAX when it contains a comma, a double quote or a newline.

inputs.name: shelfkit
inputs.intent: Use shelfkit's ISBN rule for every book: POST /books and the import answer HTTP 400 for an ISBN whose check digit is wrong. Use shelfkit's lending policy for POST /loans.

expected.extend: the import and export of books
expected.correct: the ISBN rule: firestarter's thirteen digits become shelfkit's checksum, by the intent
expected.fill: LendingPolicy, when loans are not built on arrival; otherwise an overlap, and the case records which
expected.conflict: the title limit: 120 in firestarter's seed, 200 in shelfkit's CatalogueEntry; no intent decides it

decisions.by: operator, scripted so runs stay repeatable
